items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself.

ctx.x: What was his name again? Carter?

Earl Carter. Yeah. A Chicago drummer. He filled in for two weeks. And Spobara comes up and takes his place. This man knew that that's all the way we used him for two weeks. And we did pretty good at the Del Abbey. Then Harry James buys an entrance in the Casino Gardens with Aikenbar and Reeves. And he approaches us and offers us $75 a week to play in the Casino Gardens. We went and played the Casino Gardens. That was Kinzen Clock. And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself.…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: the trombone players sewed it up, whether he was Edwards or Christian, they sewed it up

ctx.x: That's right, they're credited with authorship. Now, will you tell me this, Nick, is there any story behind the satanic blues? In other words, these fellas didn't read too much music either. Did they take this, or did they just act a composer?

They'll give me an idea of how, why don't you make a tune on this? Well, it was a cooperative band, and it didn't make no difference whose name went on the tunes. So I played the melody, and like I say, Shields put the lace on it, and the trombone players sewed it up, whether he was Edwards or Christian, they sewed it up, and that was the way I started playing.
Well, before we play this record, let me just ask you one thing, Nick. There's been a lot of misunderstanding. The original Dixieland jazz band was composed of good friends. Isn't this so?

items.q: Now when we came back to America, we got taking Edwards back in the band

ctx.x: I forgot certain incidents at places like we played in London before we came back to America. We were asked by the British government to play at the Savoy Hotel. That was a celebration of the Peace Victory Ball. Yeah we worked to play the dance music and we went on over there after they had all the parades and all kinds of ceremonies in the street all day.
